To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lymphoblastoid cells derived from patients with xeroderma pig- mentosum are useful for biochemical studies of DNA repair.
Epstein-Barr virus-transformed lymphocytes of xerodermapigmentosum patients have the characteristics of xeroderman pigmentosum.

lymphoblastoid cells established after transformation of peripheral lymphocytes with Epstein-Barr Virus retain the same degree of defect in unscheduled DNA synthesis and UV sensitivity as do dermal fibroblast cultures from the same patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of lymphoblastoid cells from XP patients.
the establishment and characterization of lymphoblastoid lines from patients with the genetic disease xeroderma.
the establishment of permanent lines of xerosoma pigmentosa cells and the use of these cell lines for studies on the mechanism for DNA repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XP cell lines established by the method of Epstein-Barr virus transformation are suitable for biochemical studies of XP.

the XP cell lines established by the method described in the present report have all the properties expected of a permanent cell line and can be used for studies on the mechanism and regulation of DNA repair in XP cells.
the lymphoblastoid cells of XP patients are as defective in the DNA repair process as the fibroblasts of these individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Epstein-Barr virus-transformed lymphoblastoid cells from XP patients are a useful model system in the study of the molecular basis of the disease.

the Epstein-Barr virus transformation of peripheral lymphocytes of XP patients is a useful method of establishing permanent XP cell lines, and that XP cells transformed by Epstein-Barr can be maintained in suspension cultures.

Epstein-Barr virus transformation is a convenient method to establish permanent lines of XP cells, and the XP and normal lymphoid cell lines thus established are useful tools for biochemical and genetic analyses of the mechanism of DNA damage repair in XP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lymphoblastoid cells from XP patients are a good model for studying the molecular mechanism of DNA repair in XP.
the characteristics of XP are not altered in lymphoblastoid cells.

the properties related with XP are not altered after transformation with Epstein-Barrera virus and are the identical in degrees of defect because are those of derma fibroblasts of the respective individuals.
